meta.headline: How high is US inflation in 2026, and what is pushing it up?
meta.seoTitle: How high is US inflation, and what is driving it?

dek.text: Consumer prices rose 3.7 percent in the year to September 2026: less than half the 2022 peak, but higher than when the administration took office, with gasoline behind over half of September's monthly rise.

assertions.text: The CPI-U rose 3.7 percent over the 12 months to September 2026.
The 12-month CPI-U change peaked at 9.1 percent in June 2022 and was 3.7 percent in September 2026, less than half the peak.
The 12-month CPI-U change was 3.0 percent in January 2025 and higher, 3.7 percent, in September 2026.
BLS reported the gasoline index rose 9.1 percent in September 2026, accounting for over half of the monthly all items increase.

description.text: US consumer prices rose 3.7 percent in the year to September 2026. How that compares with the 2022 peak and the Fed goal, and what is driving it.

assertions.text: The CPI-U rose 3.7 percent over the 12 months to September 2026.
The 12-month CPI-U change peaked at 9.1 percent in June 2022 and was 3.7 percent in September 2026, less than half the peak.

sections.name: hook
sections.heading: Is there inflation, and is it high?

sentences.text: Speaking at a Montana rally in October, President Trump said "we have very little inflation".

assertions.text: Trump said at his Kalispell, Montana rally that we have very little inflation.

sentences.text: A CBS News politics reporter answered with another yardstick: "inflation is higher than when he took office".

assertions.text: A CBS News politics reporter said inflation is higher than when Trump took office.

quote.text: inflation is higher than when he took office
quote.speaker: CBS News

sentences.text: Both sides can point at the same government price index, so the quarrel is less about the data than about what each side measures it against.
This article takes those comparisons in turn, then asks what is pushing prices up this year.

sections.name: question-1
sections.heading: How high is US inflation right now, compared with the target, the past and the 2022 peak?

sentences.text: The flattest version of the low-inflation case is Trump's own: "we don't have inflation".

assertions.text: Trump said we don't have inflation.

sentences.text: The Bureau of Labor Statistics' September report contradicts it: the consumer price index for all urban consumers rose 0.6 percent in September, seasonally adjusted, and 3.7 percent over 12 months.

assertions.text: The CPI-U rose 0.6 percent on a seasonally adjusted basis in September 2026 and 3.7 percent over the 12 months before seasonal adjustment.

blocks.caption: Consumer prices (CPI-U, not seasonally adjusted): the yearly rate at the months each comparison uses

rows.label: June 2022, the peak of the series
March 2024, the highest month of 2024 and 2025
January 2025, when the administration took office
April 2025, the lowest month since March 2021

sentences.text: Trump's own benchmark is the past: "we inherited the worst inflation in history", he told the same rally.

assertions.text: Trump said at the Montana rally that his administration inherited the worst inflation in history.

quote.text: we inherited the worst inflation in history
quote.speaker: Trump

sentences.text: The table cannot rank all of history, but it does show the peak he means: 9.1 percent in June 2022, against 3.7 percent now, less than half of it.

assertions.text: The 12-month CPI-U change peaked at 9.1 percent in June 2022 and was 3.7 percent in September 2026, less than half the peak.

sentences.text: Of January's reading, the YouTube channel The Right-Wing Populist said it was "the lowest we've had in five years".

assertions.text: The Right-Wing Populist said January CPI was the lowest we've had in five years.

quote.text: the lowest we've had in five years
quote.speaker: The Right-Wing Populist

sentences.text: That was nearly right: since March 2021 only April 2025's 2.3 percent came in under January's 2.4 percent, which was close to the 2.5 percent of January 2020.

assertions.text: The 12-month CPI-U change was 2.4 percent in January 2026; since March 2021 only April 2025, at 2.3 percent, was lower; in January and February 2020 it was 2.5 and 2.3 percent.

sentences.text: Whether that counts as low by historical standards depends on how much history you have: the government series cited here begins in 2020, so it can set January 2026 against the pandemic years but not against earlier decades.

assertions.text: The CPI-U 12-month series cited runs from January 2020; within it, January 2026 was among the lowest readings since March 2021.
qualifications: This sentence is the limit: the cited series begins in 2020.

sentences.text: Within that record, calling January low was fair, but the verdict rests on this short span and is held with moderate confidence.

assertions.text: January 2026 was low within the 2020-2026 CPI-U series.
qualifications: s11 says the series begins in 2020.

sentences.text: By September that description no longer fitted: 3.7 percent was above every month of 2024 and 2025.

assertions.text: The 12-month CPI-U change in September 2026, 3.7 percent, was higher than every monthly reading in 2024 and 2025.

sentences.text: Measured from January 2025, the month the administration took office, the rate has risen from 3.0 percent, which is the comparison the CBS reporter was making.

assertions.text: The 12-month CPI-U change was 3.0 percent in January 2025 and higher, 3.7 percent, in September 2026.

sentences.text: Trump also offers a shorter window: "we're at 1.7% inflation for the last three months", he told reporters.

assertions.text: Trump told reporters we're at 1.7% inflation for the last three months.

quote.text: we're at 1.7% inflation for the last three months
quote.speaker: Trump

sentences.text: The seasonally adjusted index does not bear that out: it climbed from 332.568 in June to 336.298 in September, a pace of about 4.6 percent a year.

assertions.text: Seasonally adjusted CPI-U rose from 332.568 in June to 336.298 in September 2026, an annualized pace of about 4.6 percent.

sentences.text: Move the window back to end in August and the pace drops to about 0.2 percent a year, because the index fell 0.4 percent in June.

assertions.text: Seasonally adjusted CPI-U went from 333.979 (2026-05) to 334.131 (2026-08), an annualized pace of about 0.2 percent, after a fall of 0.4 percent in June.

blocks.caption: The seasonally adjusted price index around the summer of 2026: the June dip makes a window ending in August look flat.

sentences.text: At its September press conference the Federal Reserve said "for more than five years, inflation has been running above target".

assertions.text: The Federal Reserve said at its September press conference that for more than five years inflation has been running above target.

quote.text: for more than five years, inflation has been running above target
quote.speaker: Federal Reserve

sentences.text: The Committee's September statement says inflation remains elevated against its 2 percent goal.

assertions.text: The FOMC's September 2026 statement says inflation remains elevated and names the Committee's 2 percent goal.
qualifications: The sentence says only what the goal is; it does not say how long inflation has been above it (s20 carries the CPI record).

sentences.text: Its participants project 3.7 percent for 2026 on PCE, the price index for personal consumption expenditures, against a longer-run rate of 2.0 percent.

assertions.text: FOMC participants' September 2026 projection for PCE inflation (fourth quarter of the previous year to fourth quarter of 2026) is 3.7 percent, against a longer-run rate of 2.0; PCE inflation is the change in the price index for personal consumption expenditures.
qualifications: A projection, not a reading: 'expect' and 'over 2026' in the sentence.

sentences.text: The statement and the projection do not cover earlier years; the consumer price index does, and its yearly rate has been at least 2.3 percent in every month with a reading since March 2021, though the Fed's goal is set on a different index, PCE, so this record shows the trend rather than the target's own measure.

assertions.text: The 12-month CPI-U change has been at least 2.3 percent in every month with a reading from March 2021 through September 2026.
qualifications: The sentence says the FOMC documents do not cover earlier years and that the multi-year record is on the consumer price index.

sentences.text: A slower rate is also not the same thing as lower prices.
Even The Right-Wing Populist, which welcomed January's figure, said "prices are technically expanding, but the actual rate is decreasing".

assertions.text: The Right-Wing Populist said prices are technically expanding, but the actual rate is decreasing.

quote.text: prices are technically expanding, but the actual rate is decreasing
quote.speaker: The Right-Wing Populist

sentences.text: The record after the peak shows it: from January 2023 to September 2024 the yearly rate fell from 6.4 percent to 2.4 percent, while the index itself rose from 299.17 to 315.301, about 5.4 percent.

assertions.text: From January 2023 to September 2024 the 12-month CPI-U change fell from 6.4 percent to 2.4 percent while the CPI-U level rose from 299.17 to 315.301, about 5.4 percent.

sections.name: question-2
sections.heading: What is pushing US inflation up in 2026: gasoline, tariffs, or prices across the board?

sentences.text: The yearly rate eased from 3.0 percent in September 2025 to 2.4 percent in January and February 2026, then climbed to 4.2 percent by May.

assertions.text: The 12-month CPI-U change eased from 3.0 percent in September 2025 to 2.4 percent in January and February 2026, then rose to 3.3, 3.8 and 4.2 percent in March, April and May 2026.
qualifications: s27 says the price tables show the rise but do not name its cause.

blocks.caption: Yearly change in all consumer prices and in core prices (all items less food and energy), CPI-U not seasonally adjusted, 2026

sentences.text: NBC News blamed the turn on the war: "but then with the Iran war prices shot up".

assertions.text: NBC News said that with the Iran war prices shot up.

quote.text: but then with the Iran war prices shot up
quote.speaker: NBC News

sentences.text: The government price tables record the rise but do not name what caused it.

assertions.text: The CPI-U series shows the 2026 rise in the 12-month rate but does not name its cause.
qualifications: This sentence is the qualification: the tables do not attribute the rise to the war.

sentences.text: Gasoline jumped: its index rose 24.9 percent in March, 11.1 percent in April and 8.6 percent in May, then fell 9.7 percent in June, though the tables do not say how much of the overall rise that explains.

assertions.text: The CPI-U gasoline index (NSA) rose 24.9 percent in March 2026, 11.1 percent in April and 8.6 percent in May, then fell 9.7 percent in June.
qualifications: The sentence says the tables do not give gasoline's share of the overall rise; no basket weight is cited.

blocks.caption: Monthly change in the gasoline price index through the spring of 2026.

sentences.text: The September report is more direct: gasoline rose 9.1 percent that month and accounted for over half of the month's increase.

assertions.text: BLS reported the gasoline index rose 9.1 percent in September 2026, accounting for over half of the monthly all items increase.

blocks.caption: The September 2026 consumer price report, by component (the monthly figures are seasonally adjusted)

rows.label: Core (all items less food and energy)

sentences.text: Others say the rise is wider than fuel; an economist on PBS NewsHour said "the war in Iran is not causing medical care, dental care, toys, apparel".

assertions.text: An economist on PBS NewsHour said the war in Iran is not causing medical care, dental care, toys, apparel price rises.

quote.text: the war in Iran is not causing medical care, dental care, toys, apparel
quote.speaker: PBS NewsHour

sentences.text: The report backs part of that: used cars and trucks, airline fares, medical care and apparel were among the indexes that rose in September.

assertions.text: BLS reported that indexes that increased in September 2026 include used cars and trucks, airline fares, medical care and apparel.
qualifications: s31 says core rose 0.3 percent on the month, the same as August, so the spread is modest.

sentences.text: But core prices rose 0.3 percent on the month, the same as in August, so prices rose in more places without the monthly core rate speeding up, though the yearly core rate edged up from 2.4 to 2.6 percent.

assertions.text: BLS reported the all items less food and energy index rose 0.3 percent in September 2026, as it did in August, and 2.6 percent over the year, up from 2.4 percent over the year to August.
qualifications: This sentence is the qualification: the monthly core rate did not accelerate.

sentences.text: Some economists put the underlying rate higher; in June, Michael Strain said "I think underlying inflation is around 3%".

assertions.text: Michael Strain said in June, I think underlying inflation is around 3%.

quote.text: I think underlying inflation is around 3%
quote.speaker: Michael Strain

sentences.text: Core inflation has sat a little below that all year, between 2.4 and 2.9 percent, and it had slowed from 3.1 percent in July and August 2025 to 2.4 percent in August 2026 before rising to 2.6 percent in September.

assertions.text: The 12-month core CPI-U change ran between 2.4 and 2.9 percent from January to September 2026, down from 3.1 percent in July and August 2025, and rose to 2.6 percent in September after 2.4 in August.
qualifications: The sentence carries the qualification: 'around three' overstates core slightly, and core did decelerate before rebounding.

sentences.text: Housing still runs hot: the shelter index rose 3.2 percent over the year, faster than the 2.6 percent for core.

assertions.text: The CPI shelter index rose 3.2 percent over the 12 months to September 2026, faster than the 2.6 percent for all items less food and energy.

sentences.text: On tariffs, New York Fed economists estimate a cumulative contribution of around 2.9 percentage points to price changes for the goods in their sample by February 2026.

assertions.text: A New York Fed study estimates tariffs made a cumulative contribution of around 2.9 percentage points to price changes for the goods in its sample by February 2026.
qualifications: s37 says the estimate is relative to less-exposed goods, illustrative, and covers only the sampled goods.

sentences.text: The authors say the estimate compares those goods with less-exposed ones, should be read as illustrative of the size of the increase for the goods studied, and so cannot say how much of core or overall inflation tariffs explain.

assertions.text: The study identifies the tariff effect relative to less-exposed goods, says the counterfactual should be read as illustrative of the magnitude for the goods in its sample, and so does not measure tariffs' contribution to overall inflation.
qualifications: This sentence is the qualification for s36.

sections.name: close
sections.heading: How to read the next inflation claim

sentences.text: Most of the people quoted here are reading the same index; what they disagree about is the yardstick.
When you hear that inflation is high or low, ask what it is being compared with, and over which months.
To judge whether a rise will outlast fuel prices, look at core rather than the headline, and remember that a falling rate still means prices that are going up.

assertions.text: A falling inflation rate does not mean falling prices: the CPI-U level kept rising while the 12-month rate fell from January 2023 to September 2024.
